title: The Problems with “Synthetic Cannabis” Begin With Its Name

content_html_sanitized:
The Irish newspaper, The Irish Examiner, has published an article about “Synthetic Cannabis”

“Synthetic cannabis HHC is being sold in Irish shops despite expert warnings of addiction, psychosis, and teen hospitalisations.”

“The product, a semi-synthetic version of a natural cannabinoid found in cannabis, can be used in vapes or in jelly edibles. It emulates the effects of THC (tetrahydrocannabinol), the narcotic component present in cannabis plants. (Emphasis added. Narcotic??? Synthetic journalism?)

From Drugs.ie the official Irish agency trying to educate their people about “drugs”. “Synthetic cannabinoids are a growing family of man-made chemicals that mimic the effects of THC, the main psychoactive constituent in cannabis. Like THC, they bind to the same receptors in the body.

There is currently a risk of synthetic cannabinoids appearing in herbal (plant material),vape/liquid, edibles sold as THC products in Ireland. As of January 2023, the HSE advise the public that there is a high level of risk associated with THC edibles currently being sold on the drug market in Ireland, as they may not contain THC but instead contain a synthetic cannabinoid.

These products do not contain cannabis but are intended to produce similar, more potent effects. However, they should not be confused with cannabis.”

The headline story is obviously not a new problem,  but they cannot report on it accurately, because they would have to explain that this problem is entirely a artifact of cannabis prohibition. The simple fact is that black markets have no quality controls. The “synthetic cannabis” may not even be a “synthetic cannabinoid”, and it is certainly not a uniquely Irish problem.

From The UK:“Synthetic cannabinoids: the number of synthetic cannabinoid seizures increased by 60%, from 637 seizures to 1,020 seizures, compared to the previous year. NPS powders: the number of NPS powder seizures increased by 17%, from 181 seizures to 211 seizures, compared to the previous year.”

From Germany: Characterising a New Cannabis Trend: Extensive Analysis of Semi-Synthetic Cannabinoid-Containing Seizures From Germany

This article from the Emergency Medicine Residents' Association, Synthetic Cannabinoids Highlight the Need to Abandon the War on Drugs explains the fundamental problem from a public health perspective.

Finally, let me point out a fundamental problem with the public health debate about cannabis.

It is generally agreed that adolescents should not use cannabis or alcohol, but when an adolescent is reported to have cannabis related problems, and both real and “synthetic” cannabis are sold in the same black market, how do these “experts” know if the problem was caused by real cannabis or by some “synthetic.”

See Politicized Psychiatry and the Rehab Rackets

At least in this report from Ireland, the fact that it was bought from unethical retailers makes it clear that it was a “synthetic.” Otherwise, we would be reading about how this newly “potent cannabis” was causing reefer madness.
